ops.en: THE PLANT. MALE et amtechot ha-anashim... VE-SIM kesef ish — the governor scripts the third silver-return; the order is the trial's stage-directions, pushed on the steward who executes without question.

THE RECEIPT. va-yaas KI-DVAR yosef asher diber — the according-to- the-word clause pops the plant-order in its own breath (the steward's second clean receipt, after 43:17); ve-et GEVII gevia ha- kesef — 'MY cup, the silver cup': the possessive doubled before the object (the letter grips the prop); gevii with no restraining-stroke on the vav per MS (asserted [G67-13]).
THE FALSE DAWN. ha-boqer OR — the morning 'was light': the only wholly serene clause the trial allows; the sending (shulchu) is the trap's release-spring.

THE PURSUIT. QUM REDOF acharei ha-anashim VE-HISAGTAM — arise, pursue, overtake, say: four verbs scripted; lama shilamtem RAA tachat TOVA — the evil-for-good formula: the machine notes the accusation is the governor's own biography inverted (he repays good for evil across the span).

THE DIVINING CLAIM. ve-hu NACHESH YENACHESH bo — the doubled divining-verb put in the steward's mouth (and Joseph will repeat it in his own, 44:15): the serpent-root (nachash, the garden's word) worn as the mask's credential — the machine files the mask's theology against 40:8 and 41:16 (interpretations belong to God).

THE ONLY OTHER PLACE THE TORAH USES THIS WORD, IT OUTLAWS THE PRACTICE [claim G67-22, machine-checked]. Onkelos writes at both seats that he thoroughly INVESTIGATES - the goblet made an instrument of inquiry rather than an oracle. Machine-checked across the whole Torah: the divination root in this form stands at exactly FIVE tokens across THREE verses - twice here, twice at the boast, and once at …

THE OVERTAKING [G67-08]. va-YASIGEM — the pursue-overtake-say order pops as the verse walks it; and the overtake-verb is written LEAN — its one such token in the Torah, against the full-yod rule that governs every hiriq-pointed form of this word (MS and the Ramah's rule) [VERIFIED: manifest G67-08]: the pursuit itself is clipped.
THE PROTEST. CHALILA la-avadekha — the far-be-it word (Abraham's at the Sodom argument, 18:25): the brothers reach for the patriarch's own courtroom idiom; the machine files the register-jump.

THE A-FORTIORI. hen kesef... HESHIVONU — the brothers argue from their own record (the returned silver of 43:21): the law-grammar qal-va-chomer in narrative dress; the machine files the argument- form.

THIS VERSE IS THE TRADITION'S OWN FIRST EXAMPLE OF THE RULE THIS MACHINE CITES EVERYWHERE [claim G67-21, machine-checked; middah I1]. Ten arguments from the lesser to the greater are said to be written in Scripture, and the census OPENS here - the silver we returned; how then should we steal? Machine-checked on the Torah members: the two-particle frame the first two share stands at exactly THREE T…

THE SOFTENING [G67-09]. gam ata khe-divrekhem KEN hu — the steward accepts 'according to your words' and then rules BELOW them: no death, one slave, the rest CLEAN (neqiyim) — a sentence revised downward by its executor (the span's mercy-grammar rehearsing its master's). NEQIYIM written with ONE yod — its one such token here: the Hilleli one yod, the Yerushalmi two, all our books one, and MS untan…

THE LOWERING [G67-07]. va-yimaharu VA-YORIDU — the lower-verb full- vav-lean-yod, exactly TWICE so in the Torah: the bags lowered here, and the spies' fruit 'brought down' to the camp (Deut 1:25) [VERIFIED: manifest G67-07] — both descents carry evidence; an old scroll-correction's variant (va-yerdu) is the reading the Masorah locks out (framed). The search-scene's speed (va-yimaharu) is innocence…

THE FINDING. ba-gadol hechel u-va-qaton kila — the search walks the birth-order the table sat (43:33): the trial quotes the feast; va- yimatze... BINYAMIN — the found-verb lands on the lean-written son (binyamin without yod, the demanded-son spelling, asserted under G65-02's census law).

THE ACCUSATION REACHES BACK THIRTEEN CHAPTERS [credit at its home seat]. The brothers taunt - thief, son of a thief - reaching back to the mother's theft of the household gods, and the answer comes straight: is the man who sold Joseph here? are there goats here? The retort names the two crimes the accusers actually committed. A standing row seated on this verse. [folded shape: kept record]

THE TEARING. va-YIQREU simlotam — the tear-verb of the father's mourning (37:34, over the coat they dipped) now tears the SONS' garments: the garment-code closes its loop — the men who stripped a coat tear their own; the machine marks the event as the span's first involuntary act.

A MEASURE-FOR-MEASURE LEDGER DRAWS HERE [claim G67-29]. The standing table holds that those who made their father rend his garments would rend their own; this verse is its first repayment, on a clause whose plain sense is only distress. Opened at the sale block, collected here. [folded shape: kept record]

THE FALLING. va-YIPLU lefanav ARTZA — the dream-ledger's third station and its steepest: bowed (42:6), bowed twice (43:26/28), now FALLEN to the earth; the narrator heads the column 'JUDAH and his brothers' — the speech-bearer takes the file's lead three verses early.

A KINGSHIP ACCOUNTED FOR BY SPEECH ACTS, AND TWO OF THE THREE ARE IN THIS BLOCK [claim G67-28]. The standing reading counts three speeches that crowned him, the third being his proposal at the sale; this verse and the approach four verses on are the other two. Verified at the ink: all three verses stand as the reading names them, the speaker named first in each. The ledger completes on this unit's…

LIKE ME [G67-03]. ish asher KAMONI — the like-me word written LEAN, exactly THREE times in the Torah: the masked governor's divination- claim (here), the Holy One's plague-word 'there is none LIKE ME in all the earth' (Exod 9:14), and the prophet 'LIKE ME' whom Moses promises (Deut 18:15) [VERIFIED: manifest G67-03]: a mask, the Name, and the prophet share the lean skeleton — the letter's own comm…

THE GUILT FOUND [G67-02]. ha-ELOHIM MATZA et avon avadekha — Judah reads the cup as the pit's receipt (the guilt found is twenty-two years old): the span's theology spoken by the guilty. HINENU avadim — the here-we-are with BOTH nuns dageshed: the Masorah counts THREE such in the Torah and the census is exact — this surrender, the brothers' final 'here we are, your slaves' (50:18), and the doomed …

ONE VERB PULLED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS BY THE TWO MEMBERS OF THE READING [claim G67-27]. Onkelos turns the clause passive - FROM BEFORE the LORD the iniquity HAS BEEN FOUND - removing the finding from God's own hand. The chain does the reverse: the creditor has FOUND his occasion to collect the note. And the three questions of this verse are read as three ledgers at once - the first silver, the se…

THE DISMISSAL [G67-11]. ve-atem ALU le-shalom el avikhem — the governor's release-order: pushed, and NEVER obeyed — the next verse is Judah stepping closer, not the brothers going up: the queue holds the dismissal open while the great speech overturns the board (the span's structural irony, machine-recorded). ha-ISH under the pazer stroke (MS rules the great pazer; SNAPSHOT writes the pazer in- st…

THE DRAWING NEAR [G67-04]. va-YIGASH elav YEHUDA — the closed break (setuma) stands immediately before this word: the portion-seam at the step forward (named). VE-AL YICHAR apekha — 'let not your anger burn': the phrase stands exactly TWICE in the Torah, both in this cycle — Judah's plea here, and Joseph's own 'let it not burn in your eyes that you sold me' (45:5, ARMED) [VERIFIED: manifest G67-04…

ARGUMENT MODELLED AS ACCUMULATION, NOT FORCE [claim G67-25]. Counsel in the heart is deep water, and the drawer ties rope to rope, thread to thread, cord to cord until he reaches it - so he answered on every single matter, not relenting, until he reached the heart. Each clause is a knot, and the depth is reached only by adding them. [folded shape: kept record]

THE CHAIN IS RECORDED DOING WHAT THIS PROJECT DOES [claim G67-26]. Words like golden apples in silver settings, sound on every side as a wheel shows its face all round - and in the same passage AKILAS THE PROSELYTE is cited BY NAME for a rival rendering of the verse. A translation named, quoted, and weighed as evidence inside the midrash, beside the translation this reading declares. The persuasio…

ONE ARGUMENT SETTLING THREE SEPARATE ACCOUNTS [claim G67-24]. Everything said from this verse until the listener breaks down is read as conciliation three ways simultaneously - toward the brother he once sold, toward the brothers, and toward the boy himself: as I give my life for you, so would I for your brother. The repentance the sale has been waiting on, delivered in a single speech. Carried wi…

THE DUEL ENDS IN RECOGNITION, NOT IN FORCE [claim G67-30]. A roar carrying four hundred parsangs until a nephew leapt from Canaan to join it; both men roaring as lions until the warriors' teeth fell out; the ground kicked into furrows; a stone pillar kicked into pebbles. The signs of the rage are themselves recorded as disputed. And the resolution is a judgment rather than a blow - the sword would…

THE RETELLING OF RETELLINGS. adoni SHAAL — Judah retells 43:7's retelling of 42:13's telling: the corpus's deepest quotation-nest (three frames), and the variance-file opens at once — the speech will add what no narrator recorded.

THE CHILD AND THE LEFT-ALONE [G67-05]. ve-YELED zequnim — the child- word stands TWICE in the Torah: the old-age child here and Lemech's 'a CHILD for my wound' (4:23) [VERIFIED: manifest G67-05]; VE-YOTER hu levado — and the left-alone verb stands twice: 'and Jacob was LEFT alone' at the wrestling (32:25) and Benjamin 'LEFT alone of his mother' here (asserted): one verse carrying both pair-words —…

BROUGHT DOWN [G67-01 — THE UNIT'S MARQUEE]. HORIDUHU elai — 'bring him down to me': the form stands exactly TWICE in the Torah, and its partner is the span's own wound — 'the Ishmaelites BROUGHT HIM DOWN there' (39:1, Joseph into Egypt) [VERIFIED: manifest G67-01]: the same skeleton carries the brother sold down and the brother demanded down; the Ramah rules both spellings letter-identical (full v…

THE ADDED DEATH. ve-azav et aviv VA-MET — 'and he would die': the clause no earlier verse spoke (42:38 feared harm, not death-by- parting): the retelling escalates, and the machine files whose death the pronoun leaves open — the lad's or the father's (the readings split, named-only).

THE FACE-CLAUSE. lo TISFUN lirot panai — the not-again verb lean- vav-lean-yod with every book and the Hilleli (its Deuteronomy partner named; asserted [G67-13]); ha-QATAN with the qof dageshed (checked [G67-13]): the third quotation of the carrying demand — Judah has made the queue his text.
THE RELAY. va-naged lo — the tell-verb (the full/lean file of G65-06) carries the demand up to Canaan: the speech now retells gen_66's opening.

THE REQUOTE [G66-03 CLOSED]. SHUVU shivru lanu meat okhel — Jacob's superseded demand (43:2) quoted verbatim, and the return-verb LEAN again exactly as the Ramah rules the pair (43:2 / 44:25 both lean; asserted): the dead demand survives as testimony — the queue's ghost speaks in the speech.
THE CONDITION REQUOTED. lo nukhal LAREDET — gen_66's strike-clause (43:5) in the speech's frame: the descent-verbs pile (yarod yaradnu, nerda, lo nered, laredet) — the span's grammar keeps falling.

THE TWO. shenayim yalda li ISHTI — 'MY WIFE bore me two': Jacob's four wives reduced to one in his own quoted mouth (Rachel the wife; the readings on the household's own ranking, named): the speech lets the father's heart draw the family tree.

TORN, TORN. akh TAROF TORAF — Jacob's verdict over the dipped coat (37:33, gen_60's dead-open haker-na file) quoted BY Judah TO the torn one: the speech hands Joseph his own death-certificate with the ink still wrong; ve-lo reitiv AD HENA — 'until now': the word true in a sense the speaker cannot see (he is looking at him), filed as the letter's cruelest dramatic irony.

THE SAME WORDS RE-SPOKEN SEVEN CHAPTERS LATER GET THE SAME VERDICT [claim G67-23, machine-checked]. The father quotes himself, and Onkelos writes surely he is KILLED - the identical rendering recorded at the original scene. Machine-checked: the doubled pair stands at exactly TWO Torah seats, both about this one son; the only other occurrence of the first word is followed by a different form, in th…

THE SECOND GRAY HAIR [G65-08 CLOSED; G67-06]. ve-HORADTEM et SEVATI be-raa sheola — the gray-hair word's second and last token (42:38 / 44:29, the Ramah's file census-exact, both full, both Sheol-bound); and the bring-down verb VE-HORADTEM stands THREE times in the Torah: the father's dread twice (42:38 in sorrow, 44:29 in evil) and — one chapter ahead — the sons' JOY-command 'bring my father down…

THE HARM-WORD TAKES ITS THIRD AND LAST NARRATIVE SEAT HERE. Onkelos renders it DEATH again, holding the decision across the block seam. Machine-checked at the previous unit: the word stands at exactly five Torah seats - these three, and the two verses of the miscarriage law where the whole penalty structure turns on it. Three narrative seats and two legal ones, and nothing else in the corpus. [fol…

BOUND [G67-12]. ve-nafsho QESHURA ve-nafsho — the bound-word stands ONCE in the Torah [VERIFIED: manifest G67-12]; Scripture's pair is 'folly bound in the heart of a lad' (Prov 22:15, named — the Kitzur reads the lad's folly against the father's love, and the binding holds either way): one soul knotted to one soul, said by the brother who once untied a son from a father for silver.

THE TRANSLATION SUPPLIES THE PREMISE THE SPEECH RUNS ON [claim G67-31]. The binding idiom becomes 'his soul is AS BELOVED TO HIM AS HIS OWN' - and love, not attachment, is exactly what the argument needs to be true. Two verses on, the pledge is rendered with the same technical suretyship word used at its making, so the making and the invoking carry one legal term across the block seam. [folded sha…

THE SEEING [G67-10]. ki-ROTO ki en ha-naar VA-MET — the seeing-word FULL with the Hilleli and every book (the Great Masorah's swapped lean/full note corrected by MS; the Kings partner named) [VERIFIED: manifest G67-10]; ve-horidu... et SEVAT — the gray-hair file's third form (sevat, 44:31), Jacob's hair a third time Sheol-bound: the file closes complete (G65-08).

THE SURETY CASHED [gen_66 ARMED, DISCHARGED IN PROSE]. ki avdekha ARAV et ha-naar — 43:9's pledge produced in court: Judah discloses the private oath as the speech's legal ground — the machine marks the cross-unit citation (the corpus's second witness quoting his own record, after Reuben 42:22): the plea stops being rhetoric and becomes contract.

THE SUBSTITUTION. yeshev-NA avdekha TACHAT ha-naar — 'let your servant stay INSTEAD of the lad': the instead-word (tachat) is the cycle's hinge — the brother who priced a brother (37:26-27, 'what profit') now bids himself as the payment; pushed on the governor and left OPEN at the span's end: the answer it gets is not a receipt but an unmasking (45:1, ARMED — the corpus's settlement-links will car…

THE CLOSING. ki EKH EELE el avi — the how-question that ends the longest speech in Genesis: not innocence, not law — the father's face; pen ERE va-ra asher yimtza et avi — the find-verb (matza) that found the cup (44:12) and the guilt (44:16) aimed last at the father: the speech ends and the span holds its breath (45:1 is the next word).

THE UNIT ENDS MID-SPEECH, AND SAYS SO [claim G67-32]. This unit spans the whole chapter, so it carries the next weekly portion's opening seventeen verses under the block-boundary law - and the speech does not conclude here.
